declared.title: Long-Run Effects of Lottery Wealth on Psychological Well-Being
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « long-run effects of lottery wealth on psychological well-being » (2026-11-22)

population: Swedish lottery players surveyed 5 to 22 years after a win; prize amounts random within groups of players

findings.text: Winning a large prize raises satisfaction with life for more than a decade, with no sign of fading

support.sentence: Relative to matched controls, large-prize winners experience sustained increases in overall life satisfaction that persist for over a decade and show no evidence of dissipating over time.

findings.text: The effects on happiness and on mental health are significantly smaller than on life satisfaction

support.sentence: The estimated treatment effects on happiness and mental health are significantly smaller.

limits: a windfall of wealth, not a higher income; lottery players only; Sweden
the effect is small per amount won: 0.037 SD of life satisfaction per $100,000 after tax (NBER w24667 version, introduction)
n = 3,362 players is given by the NBER working-paper version (w24667), read by the dossier agent
a natural experiment, preregistered: prize amounts are random only within groups of players
